papers.t: A Phase 1, Open-Label, Multicenter Study of HMPL-306 in Advanced Acute Myeloid Leukemia With Isocitrate Dehydrogenase Mutations
papers.c: HMPL-306 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and promising antitumor activity in patients with IDH1- or IDH2-mutant relapsed/refractory AML.
ab: Background

No dual inhibitors of isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 and 2 (IDH1/2) are available for the treatment of relapsed/refractory acute myeloid leukemia (AML). HMPL-306 is a potent, selective dual inhibitor of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) 1 and IDH2. This phase 1 study evaluated the safety, efficacy, and pharmacokinetics of HMPL-306 in patients with IDH-mutant relapsed/refractory AML.
Methods

In the dose-escalation phase of the phase 1, open-label, multicenter study conducted in the United States and Spain (NCT04764474), patients with IDH-mutant relapsed/refractory AML were enrolled into 8 dosing cohorts and received HMPL-306 50-400 mg once-daily orally. The primary endpoints were maximum tolerated dose (MTD) and/or recommended phase 2 dose and safety.
Results

Forty-six patients were enrolled and received treatment (median age, 71 years; IDH1 mutation, 41.3%; IDH2 mutation, 56.5%; IDH inhibitor-previously treated, 26.1%). No dose-limiting toxicities occurred and MTD was not reached. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 39.1% of patients, most commonly (≥ 5%) thrombocytopenia (10.9%), differentiation syndrome (8.7%), and alanine aminotransferase increased (6.5%). At doses ≥ 150 mg (n = 35), the objective response rate was 48.6%, with median duration of objective response of 3.71 months; the rate of complete response (CR) with negative minimal residual disease, CR, and CR with partial hematological recovery was 34.3%. Antitumor activity was shown in both IDH1- and IDH2-mutant subgroups. Population pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling demonstrated maximum target inhibition at ≥ 150 mg.
Conclusions
HMPL-306 demonstrated a manageable safety profile and promising antitumor activity in patients with IDH1- or IDH2-mutant relapsed/refractory AML.

papers.t: FLT3 Mutations in Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Chronic Myelomonocytic Leukemia: A Multi-Center Analysis
papers.c: FLT3-targeted therapy was associated with longer survival in unadjusted comparisons (median OS 14.3 vs 45.9 months in MDS; 20.6 vs 35.0 months in CMML), although this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after accounting for immortal time bias introduced from variable treatment initiation timing (adjusted time-dependent HR 0.66, MDS; 0.64, CMML). These findings support early identification of FLT3-mutant MDS and CMML and highlight the need for prospective studies evaluating early therapeutic intervention in this high-risk molecular subset.
ab: FLT3 mutations are established high-risk drivers in acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but their role in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS) and chronic myelomonocytic leukemia (CMML) remains poorly defined. We assembled 115 patients with FLT3-mutant MDS (n=63) or CMML (n=52) across six academic institutions and compared clinicogenomic features and outcomes with FLT3-wildtype controls using propensity score matching and multivariable modeling. FLT3-mutant MDS and CMML displayed a proliferative phenotype, with higher white blood cell counts, increased frequency of CMML-2, and significantly higher rates of AML transformation. FLT3-mutant MDS was enriched for signaling co-mutations, such as NRAS, PTPN11, and CBL, whereas FLT3-mutant CMML showed frequent co-mutation with ASXL1 and SRSF2. FLT3 mutations were independently associated with inferior survival in both entities. After matching, FLT3-mutant MDS had worse median overall survival (OS: 19.9 vs 44.2 months, p=0.046) and leukemia-free survival (LFS: 13.8 vs 37.1 months, p=0.023). In CMML, median OS was 30.4 vs 67.2 months (p=0.017) and LFS 17.2 vs 65.6 months (p=0.014). FLT3-TKD was associated with more favorable outcomes than FLT3-ITD. FLT3-targeted therapy was associated with longer survival in unadjusted comparisons (median OS 14.3 vs 45.9 months in MDS; 20.6 vs 35.0 months in CMML), although this association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after accounting for immortal time bias introduced from variable treatment initiation timing (adjusted time-dependent HR 0.66, MDS; 0.64, CMML). These findings support early identification of FLT3-mutant MDS and CMML and highlight the need for prospective studies evaluating early therapeutic intervention in this high-risk molecular subset.

papers.t: Diagnosis and management of acute myeloid leukemia with mutated CEBPA using CEBPA-Trass, a targeted sequencing approach
papers.c: Specifically, the assessment after last consolidation showed that more than 80% of MRD-positive patients relapsed, whereas more than 80% of MRD-negative patients remained in remission for over two years. These findings suggest that CEBPA-Trass enables accurate mutation-based MRD monitoring and may improve both the diagnosis and risk stratification of patients with CEBPA-AML.
ab: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with mutated CEBPA (CEBPA-AML) was first recognized as a distinct subtype associated with favorable prognosis in 2002, and its diagnostic criteria and clinical management have been refined over time. However, several challenges remain, including the lack of accurate mutation-based methods for measurable residual disease (MRD) detection. Here, we developed a targeted next-generation sequencing approach for the CEBPA gene, which uses adapter-free PCR amplification of hotspot regions followed by paired-end sequencing to improve analytical performance (termed CEBPA-Trass), and evaluated its clinical performance in samples from the WT1-AM-04 study. CEBPA-Trass successfully detected a cryptic long insertion missed by conventional short-read sequencing. Analytical validation showed higher background for missense variants, whereas insertions or deletions involving three or more base pairs were rarely detected in negative controls and typically below 10⁻⁴, indicating high analytical specificity. Dilution experiments further showed linear detection of insertions or deletions involving three or more base pairs with a limit of detection of 10⁻⁴ -10⁻⁵, comparable to the sensitivity of real-time PCR-based MRD assays, and aligned with the in-frame mutation patterns currently associated with favorable-risk CEBPA-AML. Clinically, CEBPA-Trass-based MRD assessment significantly stratified relapse risk after both first and last consolidation therapy. Specifically, the assessment after last consolidation showed that more than 80% of MRD-positive patients relapsed, whereas more than 80% of MRD-negative patients remained in remission for over two years. These findings suggest that CEBPA-Trass enables accurate mutation-based MRD monitoring and may improve both the diagnosis and risk stratification of patients with CEBPA-AML.

papers.t: Bone Marrow Fibrosis Is Associated with Inferior Survival in Lower-Risk Myelodysplastic Syndromes and Adds Prognostic Information to IPSS-R and IPSS-M
papers.c: Moderate-to-severe bone marrow fibrosis was associated with inferior survival, particularly in lower-risk MDS, and may provide prognostic information beyond the IPSS-R and IPSS-M. These findings require confirmation in larger, externally validated cohorts.
ab: Background

While the IPSS-M has refined prognostication in myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS), the prognostic contribution of the marrow microenvironment remains incompletely captured. Although WHO 2022 recognizes bone marrow fibrosis as an adverse feature, it is not incorporated into current risk models. We evaluated whether fibrosis provides prognostic information beyond the IPSS-R and IPSS-M.
Patients And Methods

In this retrospective single-center cohort of 130 patients with primary MDS diagnosed between 2015 and 2025, we compared patients with moderate-to-severe fibrosis (MF-2/3) and those with no or mild fibrosis (MF-0/1) using risk-stratified, blast-stratified, propensity score-weighted and multivariable analyses.
Results

Forty-nine patients (37.7%) had MF-2/3, which was associated with male predominance and excess blasts. Median overall survival (OS) was 19 versus 72 months for MF-2/3 and MF-0/1, respectively (P < .001). MF-2/3 remained associated with inferior OS after adjustment for age and IPSS-R (HR 2.11, P = .017) or IPSS-M (HR 3.37, P = .021), and after inverse probability weighting (HR 2.03, P = .015). The association was concentrated in IPSS-R lower-risk MDS (HR 3.55, P < .001), was not observed in higher-risk MDS (HR 1.07, P = .904; P for interaction = .021), and persisted among patients with < 5% blasts (HR 2.22, P = .014). Adding fibrosis improved model fit (ΔAIC -4.2 for IPSS-R and -4.8 for IPSS-M) and increased the optimism-corrected C-index from 0.734 to 0.785 and from 0.767 to 0.810, respectively.
Conclusion

Moderate-to-severe bone marrow fibrosis was associated with inferior survival, particularly in lower-risk MDS, and may provide prognostic information beyond the IPSS-R and IPSS-M. These findings require confirmation in larger, externally validated cohorts.

papers.t: Early bone marrow-guided venetoclax management in frontline unfit acute myeloid leukemia: a two-stage real-world study
papers.c: Measurable residual disease (MRD) negativity, overall survival (OS), and relapse-free survival (RFS) did not differ significantly between schedules. Individualized VEN scheduling anchored to early bone marrow response may help optimize tolerability and treatment continuity in real-world AML care, warranting prospective validation.
ab: Hypomethylating agents (HMA) plus venetoclax (VEN) is a standard frontline therapy for unfit, newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML), but prolonged cytopenia and infections often limit treatment continuity. We performed a retrospective, two-stage cohort study (Jan 2021-Jun 2025) evaluating whether early bone marrow assessment-guided, response-adapted VEN management improves tolerability without compromising efficacy. Stage 1 compared patients undergoing early bone marrow assessment (cycle 1, days 14-21) with subsequent bone marrow-guided VEN adaptation versus a conventionally managed cohort. Stage 2 was a landmark analysis at cycle 3 day 1 (C3D1) comparing VEN shortening (≤ 14 days/cycle) versus continuation (> 14 days/cycle) in responding patients. Among 371 evaluable patients, 200 underwent early bone marrow-guided management, yielding lower day-56 infection-related hospitalization (24.0% vs. 37.4%; adjusted odds ratio [OR] 0.46, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.28-0.79; p = 0.005), decreased cycle 1 VEN exposure, faster cycle 2 initiation, and reduced 8-week mortality. In the stage 2 landmark cohort (n = 237), response-adapted VEN shortening (n = 137) reduced prolonged grade 4 neutropenia (41.6% vs. 61.0%; adjusted OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.23-0.73; p = 0.003) and post-landmark infection-related hospitalization (adjusted OR 0.43, 95% CI 0.23-0.84; p = 0.014). Measurable residual disease (MRD) negativity, overall survival (OS), and relapse-free survival (RFS) did not differ significantly between schedules. Individualized VEN scheduling anchored to early bone marrow response may help optimize tolerability and treatment continuity in real-world AML care, warranting prospective validation.

papers.t: Regenerative Stress Contributes to Higher Clonal Hematopoiesis with Myelodysplastic Features in Sickle Cell Disease Mice
papers.c: Our study indicates that increased HSC regenerative stress, imposed either by chronic erythropoietic demand or via autologous HSCT in SCD increases the risk of developing clonal hematopoiesis and MDS-like features. Our study provides insights into a mechanism underlying increased risk of HM in this non-malignant hematological disorder, and suggests that early intervention with curative therapies may circumvent this risk.
ab: Sickle cell disease (SCD) affects millions globally, causing significant lifelong morbidity and early death. As childhood mortality is reduced and SCD patients are surviving to adulthood, increased risk of hematological malignancy (HM) is becoming evident. Risk of therapy-related myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)/acute myeloid leukemia, following gene therapy or hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT) is also higher in SCD. The specific pathobiology that predisposes to HM is necessary to address, since survival has improved and gene therapy and HSCT are being increasingly used. We modelled the increased risk of HM in humanized SCD mice, compared to age-, sex- and strain-matched normal counterparts. We serially monitored hematopoiesis in blood and bone marrow up to 1-year-of-age and performed highly sensitive, error-corrected deep sequencing of 450 MDS/HM-associated genes. Unlike controls, SCD mice showed an 'ageing-like' phenotype with premature development of myeloid-biased hematopoiesis and hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (HSPC) mutational profile characteristic of aged mice/humans. Furthermore, a high proportion of SCD mice developed hematopoiesis with dysplastic features reminiscent of MDS morphology and higher clonal hematopoiesis burden. Imposition of regenerative stress by serial HSCT further increased HSPC mutational burden, resulting in evolution/expansion of clones harboring oncogenic driver mutations. Our study indicates that increased HSC regenerative stress, imposed either by chronic erythropoietic demand or via autologous HSCT in SCD increases the risk of developing clonal hematopoiesis and MDS-like features. Our study provides insights into a mechanism underlying increased risk of HM in this non-malignant hematological disorder, and suggests that early intervention with curative therapies may circumvent this risk.

papers.t: Effect of a Multidisciplinary Intervention on Fatigue in Lymphoma Survivors With Persistent Fatigue: A Randomized Controlled Trial (the REFUEL trial)
papers.c: A multidisciplinary intervention improved fatigue among lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue. The effect appeared to be maintained 6 months after random assignment but dissipated at 9 months.
ab: Purpose

Persistent fatigue is a prevalent, complex, and distressing late effect among lymphoma survivors. We examined the effect of a multidisciplinary intervention on fatigue among lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue.
Methods

Lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue (moderate to severe fatigue ≥6 months) were randomly assigned to usual care (n = 75) or a 12-week multidisciplinary intervention (n = 75). The intervention consisted of patient education, physical exercise, a cognitive-behavioral therapy-based program, and nutritional counseling. Total fatigue was assessed by the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (range, 0-33) 3 months after random assignment (T1; primary outcome) and at 6 (T2) and 9 (T3) months after random assignment (secondary outcomes). Other secondary outcomes were functioning and global health status/quality of life (QoL) assessed by European Organisation for Research and Treatment of Cancer QoL Questionnaire-C30. Effects were analyzed with baseline-adjusted linear mixed models for repeated measures.
Results

Compared with usual care, the intervention group reported significantly lower total fatigue at T1 (between-group difference [BGD], -3.5 [95% CI, -5.4 to -1.6]; P < .001). Secondary outcome analyses indicated that total fatigue remained lower in the intervention group at T2 (BGD, -2.4 [95% CI, -4.4 to -0.5]), but not at T3 (BGD, -0.9 [95% CI, -3.0 to 1.2]). At T1, secondary outcome analyses indicated positive intervention effects on physical (BGD, 3.8 [95% CI, 0.2 to 7.3]) and role functioning (BGD, 9.2 [95% CI, 0.9 to 17.5]) and global health status/QoL (BGD, 9.5 [95% CI, 3.5 to 15.4]), but not on social (BGD, -0.1 [95% CI, -7.4 to 7.3]), emotional (BGD, 5.6 [95% CI, 0.0 to 11.3]), or cognitive functioning (BGD, 3.5 [95% CI, -3.3 to 10.2]).
Conclusion
A multidisciplinary intervention improved fatigue among lymphoma survivors with persistent fatigue. The effect appeared to be maintained 6 months after random assignment but dissipated at 9 months.

papers.t: Alectinib as Neoadjuvant Treatment in Potentially Resectable Stage III Anaplastic Lymphoma Kinase-Positive Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: ALNEO Phase II Trial (GOIRC-01-2020-ML42316)
papers.c: The ALNEO study met its primary end point, suggesting perioperative alectinib as a feasible and active approach in potentially resectable stage III ALK-positive NSCLC.
ab: Purpose

Stage III non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a heterogeneous disease with no single definitive therapeutic approach. The role of neoadjuvant tyrosine kinase inhibitors in stage III ALK-positive NSCLC remains unknown. The ALNEO study evaluated the activity and safety of perioperative alectinib in this population.
Patients And Methods

ALNEO is an open-label, single-arm, multicenter phase II study enrolling treatment-naïve patients with potentially resectable stage III ALK-positive NSCLC. Patients received neoadjuvant alectinib 600 mg twice daily for 8 weeks, followed by surgery and adjuvant alectinib for up to 96 weeks. The primary end point was major pathologic response (MPR; ≤10% residual viable tumor cells) assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included pathologic complete response (pCR), objective response rate (ORR), event-free survival (EFS), disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and safety.
Results

From May 2021 to July 2024, 33 patients were enrolled. The median age was 62 years (range, 33-79), 70% were female, and 52% were never smokers. Clinical stage was IIIA in 64% and IIIB in 36%. All patients completed neoadjuvant treatment, and 28 (85%) underwent surgery, most commonly lobectomy (75%). R0 resection was achieved in 24 (86%). MPR was observed in 14 patients (42%; 95% CI, 26 to 61), including four pCRs (12%; 95% CI, 3 to 28). ORR was 67%. Adjuvant treatment was initiated in 26 (79%) patients. After a median follow-up of 26.8 months, median EFS, DFS, and OS were not reached; six patients (18%) experienced disease recurrence. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 9% and 27% of patients during neoadjuvant and adjuvant treatment, respectively.
Conclusion
The ALNEO study met its primary end point, suggesting perioperative alectinib as a feasible and active approach in potentially resectable stage III ALK-positive NSCLC.

papers.t: Fixed-duration glofitamab in patients with relapsed or refractory follicular lymphoma: Results from a Phase 1/2 study
papers.c: Glofitamab represents an accessible off-the-shelf therapy for patients with R/R FL, including those with high-risk disease, and an important combination partner for the treatment of R/R FL. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03075696.
ab: More effective options are needed to personalize treatment for relapsed/refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL) by balancing efficacy, safety, and accessibility. We report efficacy and safety of glofitamab, a CD20xCD3 T-cell engaging bispecific antibody, from a Phase 1/2 study in patients with R/R FL after ≥2 prior therapies. Overall, 61 patients were enrolled at the recommended Phase 2 dose of glofitamab (target dose, 30 mg). The overall response rate was 85.2% (95% confidence interval [CI] 73.8-93.0), and complete response (CR) rate was 77.0% (95% CI 64.5-86.9). After a median follow-up of 29.3 months, the median duration of CR was 40.2 months (95% CI 20.0-not estimable [NE]). Median progression-free survival was 21.4 months (95% CI 11.4-NE) and the 24-month progression-free survival rate was 49.0%. The most common adverse event was cytokine release syndrome (62.3%; all Grade ≤2). Immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome rates were low (6.5%; Grade ≤2, 4.9%; Grade 3, 1.6%). Patients had high rates of undetectable minimal residual disease at their first tumor assessment (Cycle 3) (76.3%), which lasted beyond the end-of-treatment (EOT). Immuno-recovery occurred 12-18 months after EOT in patients with ongoing remission, and T-cell count was not impacted by glofitamab treatment. Fixed-duration glofitamab monotherapy induces durable responses with manageable safety. Glofitamab represents an accessible off-the-shelf therapy for patients with R/R FL, including those with high-risk disease, and an important combination partner for the treatment of R/R FL. ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03075696.

papers.t: Lenalidomide and rituximab for relapsed/refractory follicular lymphoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.c: R2 at first relapse is effective across rituximab sensitivity profiles. Triplet combinations built on the R2 backbone improve efficacy but require careful patient selection and monitoring due to higher toxicity risks.
ab: Lenalidomide (len) and rituximab (R2) is standard second-line therapy for follicular lymphoma (FL), and the backbone and comparator for several new therapies. This systematic review and meta-analysis of R2 or len-anti-CD20 monoclonal antibodies aims to clarify efficacy across trials, and to evaluate the benefit of triplet therapies including R2. Across 24 treatment arms involving 2245 patients, 63% received R2 or len-anti-CD20 and 37% received it with an additional agent. For R2/len-anti-CD20, the overall response rate (ORR) was 75.9% (95% CI 72.1-79.3, p = 0.0092; I2 = 53.5%), and complete response rates (CR), 39.6% (95% CI 32.4-47.3, p < 0.0001, I2 = 73.2%). ORRs were similar whether studies included or excluded rituximab-refractory, but CR appeared lower (28.6% vs. 42.9%). The number of prior lines of therapy did not affect response. Adding a third agent to R2 or len-anti-CD20 resulted in similar ORRs but significantly higher CR and 1- and 2-year progression-free survival appeared longer than that seen with R2. However, triplet regimens were associated with increased grade ≥3 toxicity. These findings reinforce the role of R2 in R/R FL in the modern treatment era. R2 at first relapse is effective across rituximab sensitivity profiles. Triplet combinations built on the R2 backbone improve efficacy but require careful patient selection and monitoring due to higher toxicity risks.

papers.t: First-line bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitor regimens in marginal zone lymphoma: systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.c: First-line covalent BTKi-containing regimens showed high response rates and favorable reported 24-month survival, providing useful benchmarks for prospective evaluation. Prospective comparative trials are needed to define regimen- and subtype-specific roles.
ab: The role of Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKi) in first-line systemic treatment of marginal zone lymphoma (MZL) remains uncertain. Five databases and ASH, EHA, and ESMO sources were searched through July 31, 2026. Included studies evaluated untreated adults receiving covalent BTKi-containing regimens. Thirty-three studies were included; 31 studies comprising 770 participants contributed to the objective response analysis. Random-effects pooled objective and complete response rates were 91.7% (95% CI, 88.9%-93.8%) and 68.0% (60.4%-74.8%), respectively. Twenty-four-month progression-free and overall survival were 95.5% (93.8%-96.8%) and 97.4% (90.1%-99.4%). Among reports with unspecified adverse-event attribution, the pooled grade 3 or higher proportion was 13.0% (8.3%-19.6%); adverse-event-associated discontinuation was 5.3% (1.0%-23.2%). Full-report-only sensitivity estimates were imprecise. First-line covalent BTKi-containing regimens showed high response rates and favorable reported 24-month survival, providing useful benchmarks for prospective evaluation. Prospective comparative trials are needed to define regimen- and subtype-specific roles.

papers.t: Immune-related gene expression signatures identify a subset of patients achieving durable complete response to brentuximab vedotin in relapsed/refractory Hodgkin lymphoma
Primary Mediastinal B-Cell Lymphoma in Clinical Practice: A Case-Based Approach to Unresolved Diagnostic and Therapeutic Dilemmas
papers.c: Management increasingly relies on individualized, multidisciplinary decision-making that integrates disease biology, functional imaging and patient characteristics to maximize cure while minimizing long-term toxicity. In our practice this translates into dose-intensified frontline chemoimmunotherapy rather than R-CHOP21, omission of radiotherapy after a complete metabolic response and, where these treatments are accessible, a second-line strategy built on checkpoint inhibitors and anti-CD19 CAR-T cells, with early referral for cellular therapy in refractory or early relapse.
ab: Primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma (PMBL) is a rare and biologically distinct subtype of aggressive B-cell lymphoma that predominantly affects young adults. Despite substantial therapeutic advances, several aspects of its management remain controversial, including frontline treatment selection, the role of radiotherapy, PET-based response assessment, and the optimal sequencing of immunotherapies in relapsed disease. Drawing on prospective and retrospective studies, cooperative group data, expert consensus and our own real-world experience, we present a practical case-based approach across the disease course, built around four clinical cases followed to their resolution and covering diagnosis, frontline treatment, PET-guided response assessment, pregnancy-associated disease, adolescents and young adults, relapsed or refractory disease, and long-term follow-up. We focus on decision-making where evidence remains limited, including the integration of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), CAR-T cell therapy, radiotherapy and transplantation, and the emerging role of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and radiomics. Management increasingly relies on individualized, multidisciplinary decision-making that integrates disease biology, functional imaging and patient characteristics to maximize cure while minimizing long-term toxicity. In our practice this translates into dose-intensified frontline chemoimmunotherapy rather than R-CHOP21, omission of radiotherapy after a complete metabolic response and, where these treatments are accessible, a second-line strategy built on checkpoint inhibitors and anti-CD19 CAR-T cells, with early referral for cellular therapy in refractory or early relapse.

papers.t: Predictive Value of the Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) for Engraftment Syndrome After Autologous Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in Multiple Myeloma and Lymphoma Patients (EASIX and Engraftment Syndrome in ASCT)
papers.c: While log-transformed EASIX on day 0 correlates with ES risk, its standalone discriminative performance remains modest. EASIX is best utilized as an integrated component within broader, multiparametric risk-stratification models rather than as an isolated predictor.
ab: Engraftment syndrome (ES) is a clinically challenging, hyper-inflammatory complication following autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT). The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) has emerged as a reliable biomarker for endothelial dysfunction and non-relapse mortality in allogeneic transplantation; however, its predictive utility for ES in the autologous setting has not been fully established. This study evaluated the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes of ES in patients with multiple myeloma (MM) and lymphoma, focusing on the dynamic predictive value of peritransplant EASIX scores. We retrospectively analyzed 303 adult patients with MM or lymphoma who underwent ASCT at a single center between 2015 and 2025. ES was diagnosed using the Maiolino criteria. EASIX was assessed at four time points: before conditioning, on the day of transplantation (day 0), and on days +7 and +14. The incidence of ES was 14.2%. Demographic characteristics, conditioning regimens, and infused cell doses did not differ significantly between patients with and without ES. Pre-conditioning EASIX scores were comparable between groups; however, the median EASIX score on day 0 was significantly higher in patients who subsequently developed ES (2.35 vs. 1.46; p = 0.019). In univariable logistic regression, log-transformed EASIX on day 0 was associated with ES development (OR 1.399, 95% CI 1.033-1.894), with an AUC of 0.612 (95% CI 0.524-0.700). Patients with ES had a significantly higher rate of severe (grade 3-4) diarrhea (48.8% vs. 23.1%) and prolonged post-transplant antibiotic therapy (median 12 vs. 8 days). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in progression-free or overall survival. In conclusion, engraftment syndrome significantly increases early post-transplant gastrointestinal toxicity and supportive care requirements without adversely affecting long-term survival outcomes. While log-transformed EASIX on day 0 correlates with ES risk, its standalone discriminative performance remains modest. EASIX is best utilized as an integrated component within broader, multiparametric risk-stratification models rather than as an isolated predictor.

papers.t: Clinical Characteristics and Treatment Patterns in Patients With Follicular Lymphoma Managed With Long-Term Initial Watch-and-Wait Regimen: A Danish Nationwide Real-World Study
papers.c: In conclusion, most patients remained treatment-free beyond the WAW5-timepoint. The findings support consideration of discontinuation of routine follow-up or transition to a more flexible, need-driven follow-up after WAW5, with the option of incorporating relevant risk factors to support individualized decision-making.
ab: The optimal duration of follow-up for patients with follicular lymphoma (FL) eligible for initial watch-and-wait (WAW) remains undefined. We investigated the clinical characteristics and treatment trajectory patterns in patients with FL managed by initial, continuous WAW for at least 5 years (WAW5). Patients were identified from The Danish National Lymphoma Registry and detailed information was collected from health care records. Among the 393 included WAW5-patients, 271 (69%) were still untreated after a median follow-up of 5.3 years (after WAW5-timepoint). The 2-, 5-, and 10-year cumulative incidences of treatment initiation were 16% (95% CI 12%-20%), 28% (95% CI 24%-33%) and 38% (95% CI 32%-44%), respectively. In patients with stage II-IV disease, the best subset selection method in the training cohort (7:3 random sampling) identified the multivariable Cox regression model with number of nodal areas and bone marrow involvement with the best prognostic fit for time to treatment (TTT). Based on this, the WAW5-TTT risk score was constructed. The 5-year cumulative incidence of treatment initiation in the training cohort was 46% (95% CI 35%-58%), 37% (95% CI 26%-48%), and 13% (95% CI 5%-21%) in the high-, intermediate, and low-risk WAW5-TTT groups, respectively (Gray's test p < 0.0001). Results were confirmed in the test cohort. In conclusion, most patients remained treatment-free beyond the WAW5-timepoint. The findings support consideration of discontinuation of routine follow-up or transition to a more flexible, need-driven follow-up after WAW5, with the option of incorporating relevant risk factors to support individualized decision-making.

Radiation Therapy as Salvage or Bridging Before CAR T-Cell Therapy Improves Outcomes in Aggressive B-Cell Lymphomas With Higher-Risk Features
papers.c: Radiation before CART was associated with longer PFS, less relapse at sites of bulky disease, and lower hazard of death among patients receiving salvage/bridging therapy.
ab: Introduction

Radiation therapy (RT) is a bridging option before chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CART) infusion in B-cell lymphoma. We evaluated outcomes in patients receiving RT in the 100 days preceding CART infusion, including those who received RT as salvage before leukapheresis.
Methods

We retrospectively evaluated 139 patients with aggressive B-cell lymphomas treated with CART from January 2018 to March 2022. Baseline characteristics, response, and toxicities were compared between the RT and non-RT groups. Survival was compared among the RT, systemic-only bridging, and no bridging groups.
Results

Median follow-up was 36 months. Most patients (n = 126, 91%) had diffuse large B-cell lymphoma. Seventy-four (53%) received systemic bridging alone, 13 (9%) received RT alone, and 8 (6%) received both modalities. The RT group (n = 21) had more primary refractory (71% vs. 43%, P = .02) and bulky disease (81% vs. 55%, P = .03). Among evaluable patients, overall response rates were 84% with RT vs. 61% without RT (P = .06). RT patients had less relapse at baseline sites of bulky disease (44% vs. 89%, P = .01), less grade ≥ 3 neutropenia at day +90 (0% vs. 26%, P = .01), but more grade ≥ 3 neurotoxicity (43% vs. 19%, P = .02; adjusted odds ratio 2.87, P = .04). Median progression-free survival (PFS) was longer in RT versus systemic-only bridging (15.8 months vs. 2.9, P = .03). Among patients requiring salvage/bridging therapy, RT was associated with improved overall survival (adjusted hazard ratio 0.35, P < .01).
Conclusion
Radiation before CART was associated with longer PFS, less relapse at sites of bulky disease, and lower hazard of death among patients receiving salvage/bridging therapy.

papers.t: Long-term follow-up of relapsed/refractory large B-cell lymphoma patients treated with salvage immunochemotherapy
papers.c: Time to relapse from initial diagnosis is associated with inferior survival in this cohort of R/R LBCL patients treated with salvage immunochemotherapy, although approximately one-third of patients with early relapse disease achieve prolonged DFS. Additional efforts to risk stratify R/R LBCL patients may lead to more optimal use of this curative treatment.
ab: Background

While the CORAL study demonstrated predictors of survival in patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) large B cell lymphoma (LBCL) following treatment with salvage immunochemotherapy followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT) if demonstrating chemosensitive disease, these findings have not been validated.
Objectives
To determine risk factors predictive of long-term survival outcomes in a more contemporary cohort of R/R LBCL patients.
Study Design

Retrospective chart review of R/R LBCL patients treated at the University of Pennsylvania from 2008-19 with salvage immunochemothearpy with intent to proceed with ASCT if demonstrating chemosensitive disease.
Results

For the 154 included patients, the overall response rate was 61% and complete response rate 28%. With a median follow up of 104.8 months, the estimated 8 year disease free survival (DFS) was 31% and overall survival (OS) 37%. On multivariate analysis, time to relapse from initial diagnosis <12 months vs ≥12 months was a significant predictor of second occurrence of LBCL and death at 8 years and IPI score ≥3 vs <3 for death at 8 years. Patients with time to relapse from initial diagnosis <6 months (primary refractory) experienced significantly inferior 8 year DFS (12%) as compared to those 6-12 months (32%) as well as those 6-18 months. Findings were similar for 8 year OS. Of all deaths, 7% were due to non-lymphoma causes and 8% of patients developed secondary primary malignancies.
Conclusions

Time to relapse from initial diagnosis is associated with inferior survival in this cohort of R/R LBCL patients treated with salvage immunochemotherapy, although approximately one-third of patients with early relapse disease achieve prolonged DFS. Additional efforts to risk stratify R/R LBCL patients may lead to more optimal use of this curative treatment.

ab: Nodal follicular helper T-cell lymphoma (nTFHL) is an aggressive peripheral T-cell lymphoma with challenging diagnosis and poor prognosis. This study aimed to investigate the clinicopathological characteristics and prognostic factors of nTFHL, with a focus on the role of minimal residual disease (MRD). We conducted a retrospective analysis of 120 patients with nTFHL. Median overall survival (OS) was 30.5 months (5-year OS 25.8%), and median progression-free survival (PFS) was 19.0 months (5-year PFS 16.7%). Univariate analysis identified bone marrow involvement (BMI), serous effusion, CXCL13/BCL-6/EBER positivity, elevated LDH/β2-microglobulin, > 1 extranodal site, and high-risk scores as adverse factors. In BMI patients, persistent MRD+ after first-line therapy correlated with EBER and BCL-6 expression. Notably, among patients achieving radiologic remission but remaining MRD positive, oral maintenance therapy (e.g., chidamide) significantly prolonged OS, PFS, and duration of response compared with no maintenance. Bone marrow MRD is a dynamic biomarker surpassing radiologic assessment; persistent MRD+ predicts early relapse and inferior survival. Integrating multiparameter flow cytometry into routine evaluation is essential for risk stratification, and oral maintenance therapy mitigates the poor prognosis associated with residual disease in nTFHL.

papers.t: Integrating information across datasets to improve prognostic models for patients with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
papers.c: External validation confirmed the robustness and generalizability of the BRIDGE-Cox approach. By borrowing large populationlevel data, this model addresses key limitations of existing tools and enables more reliable risk stratification for patients with DLBCL, particularly in genomically defined subpopulations.
ab: Accurate survival prediction is vital for guiding clinical decisions in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), especially for advancing precision medicine within its genomically heterogeneous subgroups. However, datasets that include both detailed clinical variables and genomic profiling are usually small. In contrast, large population-based datasets often lack multiomics data. This gap limits the development and validation of robust prognostic models in DLBCL. We developed a transfer-learning prognostic framework that leverages the external population-level information from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results program to the prognostic model for an individual-level clinical and genomic cohort. The proposed model is a Cox-model-based boosted regression with individual data for generalization and enhancement (BRIDGE-Cox) that increases predictive accuracy and reduces uncertainty. The BRIDGE-Cox model incorporates the International Prognostic Index (IPI) factors, with model training performed in the Reddy genomic dataset and external validation in an independent National Cancer Institute genomic dataset. Compared with conventional IPI-based and revised IPI-based Cox models, the BRIDGE-Cox model improved predictive performance for overall survival, achieving a higher concordance index (0.70 vs 0.66 and 0.63, respectively) and consistently higher time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curves for 2-, 3-, and 5- year survival prediction by using the repeated cross-validation in the Reddy dataset. Importantly, these gains were maintained within genomic subgroups. External validation confirmed the robustness and generalizability of the BRIDGE-Cox approach. By borrowing large populationlevel data, this model addresses key limitations of existing tools and enables more reliable risk stratification for patients with DLBCL, particularly in genomically defined subpopulations.

ab: Transformed indolent non-Hodgkin lymphoma (tiNHL) has historically been associated with poor outcomes, particularly for patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) disease. Although chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy has improved prognosis, many patients lack access or experience relapse following treatment, highlighting the need for additional therapeutic strategies. CD3×CD20 bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) are active in R/R large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), though data in tiNHL are limited. Here, we report the efficacy and safety of epcoritamab and glofitamab in patients with R/R tiNHL (N = 74) compared with those of patients with R/R de novo diffuse LBCL (DLBCL; N = 166) from 9 academic centers in the Collaborative US Bispecifics Consortium (CUBIC). With a median follow-up of 11.5 months, best overall response rate (ORR) and complete response rate (CRR) were comparable in tiNHL (50%/31%) vs de novo DLBCL (51%/34%). 12-month progression-free survival was 25% (95% confidence interval [CI], 15-39) for tiNHL vs 34% (95% CI, 27-43) for de novo DLBCL (HR, 1.15 [95% CI, 0.83-1.61]) and 12-month overall survival was 38% (95% CI, 26-55) for tiNHL vs 47% (95% CI, 39-56) for de novo DLBCL (HR, 1.08 [95% CI, 0.73-1.60]). No differences in toxicity were observed. Similar findings were found via a 1:1 propensity score matching statistical approach. In conclusion, our study revealed comparable efficacy and toxicity of BsAbs for patients with R/R tiNHL vs patients with R/R de novo DLBCL, supporting their use in this patient population.

papers.t: Characterization and impact of response to holding/bridging therapy in second-line large B-cell lymphoma patients treated with axicabtagene ciloleucel: a LYSA study from the French DESCAR-T registry
papers.c: A predictive score combining response to H/BT, international prognostic index, LDH, and CRP at infusion identified two risk groups with significantly different EFS. In conclusion, H/BT response appears to be associated with axi-cel outcomes particularly when combined to inflammatory markers and residual LDH.
ab: The optimal approach for holding or bridging therapy (H/BT) prior to second line axicabtagene ciloleucel (axi-cel) remains undefined, and the prognostic impact of response to H/BT remains debated. Here, we characterize real-world H/BT strategies and evaluate the impact of response on outcome following axi-cel infusion in the second-line setting for relapse or refractory (R/R) large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL). We included all adults with R/R LBCL within 12 months of first-line therapy who received axi-cel in the nationwide French DESCAR-T cohort (NCT04328298). The primary objective was to EFS between H/BT responders and nonresponders, as per Lugano criteria, using propensity score matching (PSM). Secondary objectives were to characterize H/BT modalities, corresponding responses, and to identify predictors of EFS at infusion. Among 566 patients included, 469 (83%) received chemotherapy-based H/BT, while 97 (17%) received a chemo-free approach, including no H/BT. Patients treated with chemotherapy-based H/BT had more advanced disease characteristics and exhibited inferior EFS compared to those receiving chemo-free approaches. After PSM, OS was significantly improved in responders versus non-responders (HR=0·70 [95% CI 0·51-0·96], p=0·0292), while the EFS benefit no longer reached statistical significance (HR=0·86 [95%CI 0·70-1·07], p=0·1739). Given that only patients ultimately receiving axi-cel were analyzed, the impact of H/BT response may have been underestimated. A predictive score combining response to H/BT, international prognostic index, LDH, and CRP at infusion identified two risk groups with significantly different EFS. In conclusion, H/BT response appears to be associated with axi-cel outcomes particularly when combined to inflammatory markers and residual LDH.

Use and Safety of Peripherally Inserted Venous Catheters Versus Central Venous Catheters for Patients With Lymphoma Receiving Frontline Anthracycline-based Chemotherapy
papers.c: Altogether, PIVs represent a viable modality for patients with lymphoma requiring anthracycline-based chemotherapy.
ab: Introduction

Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVs) for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy have the potential risk of vascular and tissue injury due to extravasation of vesicant agents. Central venous catheters (CVCs) are frequently utilized to mitigate this. This multicenter retrospective real-world analysis (RWA) evaluated complications associated with PIVs versus CVCs for the administration of anthracycline-based chemotherapy in patients with lymphoma.
Methods

We conducted a RWA across 9 US medical centers, including adults with newly diagnosed lymphoma who received anthracycline-based chemotherapy via PIV or CVC between 2010 and 2025. Detailed baseline characteristics and safety outcomes were collected, applying standard definitions for extravasation and other recognized complications. Incidence rates of safety outcomes were calculated, and multivariable Poisson regression models were applied to adjust for confounders.
Results

In total, 1776 patients were included: 1077 with CVCs, 886 with PIVs, and 187 with both. The most common diagnoses were large B-cell lymphomas, followed by Hodgkin lymphoma, and then T-cell lymphoma. In total, there were 5464 and 4049 treatment cycles in the CVC and PIV cohorts, respectively. There was one definite case of extravasation with PIV use (incidence rate 0.19 events per 1000 infusion-cycles), compared to no cases with CVC use. PIV use was more commonly associated with flare, phlebitis, and pain, whereas CVC use was more commonly associated with deep vein thrombosis; other complications were not different between cohorts. Rates of extravasation and other complications were low in both PIV and CVC cohorts.
Conclusion
Altogether, PIVs represent a viable modality for patients with lymphoma requiring anthracycline-based chemotherapy.

papers.t: Favorable Safety and Efficacy of Duvelisib Maintenance After Autologous Stem Cell Transplant in Peripheral T-cell Lymphomas
papers.c: Duvelisib maintenance after ASCT is feasible, with a manageable safety profile, and intermittent dosing improved tolerability. Efficacy findings are exploratory and support evaluation in a larger randomized trial.
ab: Introduction/Background

Post-transplant relapse is the principal cause of treatment failure in peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) after autologous stem cell transplantation (ASCT), and no maintenance therapy is approved. We evaluated duvelisib, an oral dual phosphoinositide-3-kinase (PI3K)-δ/γ inhibitor, as post-ASCT maintenance.
Patients

In this single-center phase II trial (NCT04331119), patients aged 18 to 75 with PTCL or B-cell lymphoma began duvelisib approximately day +30 after ASCT for up to 11 cycles. After a safety lead-in with continuous dosing (25 mg twice daily, days 1-28; Schedule 1), subsequent patients received intermittent dosing (days 1-14 of a 28-day cycle; Schedule 2). The primary endpoint was 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with PTCL.
Results

Seventeen patients (12 PTCL, 5 B-cell lymphoma) received duvelisib; 15 were in complete remission at ASCT. Seven patients received Schedule 1 and 10 received Schedule 2, with median treatment durations of 4.4 and 10.2 months, respectively. Grade ≥ 3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 9 patients, most commonly lymphopenia and transaminase elevation, and there were no treatment-related deaths. Three of 7 patients on continuous dosing discontinued for toxicity. Among patients with PTCL, median follow-up was 46.4 months and estimated 2-year PFS was 74.1% (95% CI, 39.1%-90.9%). Two-year overall survival among all patients was 94.1% (95% CI, 65.0%-99.1%).
Conclusions

Duvelisib maintenance after ASCT is feasible, with a manageable safety profile, and intermittent dosing improved tolerability. Efficacy findings are exploratory and support evaluation in a larger randomized trial.

papers.t: Nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma: a prognostic index developed by the T-cell project
papers.c: Outcomes for nodal PTCL remain poor with current therapy; the externally validated TCP score offers a contemporary, complementary tool for risk stratification and identification of patients at high risk of treatment failure. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03964480, NCT01142674.
ab: To characterize real-world treatment patterns and outcomes in nodal peripheral T-cell lymphoma (PTCL) and to develop and externally validate a contemporary clinical prognostic model, we analyzed patients prospectively registered in the International T-Cell Project 2 (TCP2). Between January 2018 and January 2026, 1,465 patients with PTCL were registered; 959 with nodal PTCL by the 2016 WHO classification (PTCL not otherwise specified (PTCL-NOS), systemic anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (ALCL; ALK-positive or ALK-negative), and T-follicular helper lymphoma (TFHL)) were analyzed. The primary endpoint was 2-year progression-free survival (PFS); the model was externally validated in the TCP1 cohort (n = 1,016). The cohort comprised 396 PTCL-NOS (41%), 263 TFHL (27%), 211 ALK-negative ALCL (22%), and 89 ALK-positive ALCL (9%). First-line therapy was CHOEP in 340 (37%), CHOP in 260 (29%), and brentuximab vedotin-CHP in 139 (15%); 156 underwent consolidative stem cell transplantation. After a median follow-up of 25.3 months, 2-year PFS and overall survival were 35.3% and 54.3%, respectively. In multivariate analysis, diagnosis other than ALCL, age ≥65 years, ECOG performance status ≥2, thrombocytopenia, extranodal involvement, and elevated LDH were independently associated with inferior PFS. A six-variable score using these factors stratified patients into 3 risk groups - low (score 0-1), intermediate (2-3), and high (4-6) with 2-year PFS, 65%, 33%, and 16% respectively (P < .001) and was confirmed in the TCP1 validation cohort. Outcomes for nodal PTCL remain poor with current therapy; the externally validated TCP score offers a contemporary, complementary tool for risk stratification and identification of patients at high risk of treatment failure. papers.c: Moreover, the ROS scavenger N-acetyl-L-cysteine inhibited both PS-induced ERK activation and apoptosis, positioning ROS upstream of ERK signaling. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that PS-mediates ERK-dependent proapoptotic and proautophagic signaling via ROS activity, suggesting ERK signaling as a key determinant of PS's anticancer activity in CTCL.
ab: This study investigates the role of ERK signaling in PS-induced apoptosis and autophagy. PS treatment activated MAP kinases in CTCL cells, with robust ERK activation contrasting with variable p38/JNK responses. Pharmacological ERK inhibition significantly reversed PS-mediated loss of viability, morphological and nuclear alterations, and apoptosis (PI/Annexin V). Mechanistically, ERK blockade suppressed PS-induced cleaved caspase-3, -8, -9, PARP, and γH2AX, confirming ERK drives proapoptotic cascades. PS also triggered autophagic flux, evidenced by increased LC3 and decreased Beclin1/p62, effects reversed by 3-methyladenine. ERK inhibition attenuated PS-induced MDC staining, indicating ERK-dependent autophagic cell death. Moreover, the ROS scavenger N-acetyl-L-cysteine inhibited both PS-induced ERK activation and apoptosis, positioning ROS upstream of ERK signaling. Altogether, these findings demonstrate that PS-mediates ERK-dependent proapoptotic and proautophagic signaling via ROS activity, suggesting ERK signaling as a key determinant of PS's anticancer activity in CTCL.

papers.t: RAB13 promotes diffuse large B-cell lymphoma progression and reduces lenalidomide sensitivity via PIK3CA-associated PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling
papers.c: RAB13 is associated with aggressive clinical features and poorer survival in non-GCB DLBCL and experimentally reduces LEN sensitivity in ABC-DLBCL models. These effects involve PIK3CA and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling, supporting further evaluation of RAB13 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.
ab: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is a biologically heterogeneous malignancy with variable clinical outcomes and treatment responses. Although the small GTPase RAB13 has been implicated in several cancers, its clinical significance, biological function, and relationship to lenalidomide (LEN) sensitivity in DLBCL remain unclear. Exploratory drug-sensitivity prediction was performed using the TCGA-DLBC cohort, and RAB13 expression and clinical associations were evaluated in tissue samples from 80 patients with non-GCB DLBCL. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments were conducted in two ABC-DLBCL cell lines, followed by RNA sequencing, protein-association analyses, genetic and pharmacological inhibition of PIK3CA/PI3K signaling, and xenograft studies. High RAB13 expression was associated with high-risk clinicopathological features and poorer survival in the non-GCB DLBCL cohort and was more frequent in patients with refractory or relapsed disease in the LEN-treated subgroup. In ABC-DLBCL cell models, RAB13 overexpression increased proliferation, Transwell migration and invasion, and reduced apoptosis, whereas RAB13 knockdown showed reciprocal effects. RAB13 overexpression also reduced LEN sensitivity, whereas RAB13 knockdown increased it. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses implicated PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling. RAB13 and PIK3CA were detected in the same protein complex, and PIK3CA knockdown or pharmacological PI3K inhibition attenuated RAB13-associated AKT-mTOR activation and pro-survival phenotypes. Alpelisib enhanced LEN-induced apoptosis in RAB13-overexpressing cells. In vivo, RAB13 overexpression accelerated xenograft growth, whereas RAB13 knockdown suppressed it. LEN combined with LY294002 reduced the growth of RAB13-overexpressing xenografts. RAB13 is associated with aggressive clinical features and poorer survival in non-GCB DLBCL and experimentally reduces LEN sensitivity in ABC-DLBCL models. These effects involve PIK3CA and PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling, supporting further evaluation of RAB13 as a candidate prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target.

papers.c: Whole-slide mIF (WSI) performed in 64 selected cases confirmed the adverse prognostic impact of Tregs in R2-treated patients and further showed that extra-follicular Treg localization was specifically associated with shorter PFS (HR = 2.87, 95% CI: 1.13-7.28, p = 0.020). These data suggest that high Treg infiltration by mIF is associated with inferior outcome in lenalidomide-treated FL patients and may have potential value for risk stratification.
ab: The prognostic impact of the tumour microenvironment in follicular lymphoma (FL) remains controversial. To adress this, we analysed FL samples from patients enrolled in the rituximab lenalidomide versus any chemotherapy (RELEVANCE) trial using RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF). RNA-seq analysis (n = 354) showed that regulatory T-cell (Treg) signatures were associated with shorter PFS in the whole cohort (HR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.01-2.41, p = 0.044), particularly in patients treated with rituximab-lenalidomide (LEN) (R2, HR= 1.84, 95% CI: 1-3.37, p = 0.046) but not with rituximab-chemotherapy (R-chemo, HR = 1.33, 95% CI: 0.71-2.48, p = 0.365). mIF analysis on tissue microarrays (TMA) (n = 394) showed that high infiltration of CD3+/CD4+/FOXP3+ Tregs was associated with shorter PFS in the overall cohort (HR = 1.951, CI: 1.259-3.024, p = 0.0023 log-rank test), particularly in the R2 arm (HR = 2.3, CI: 1.2-4.5, p = 0.0097 log-rank test) and remained significant after FL-International Prognostic Index (FLIPI) adjustment (HR = 1.843; 95% CI: 1.1-2.8, p = 0.006). Whole-slide mIF (WSI) performed in 64 selected cases confirmed the adverse prognostic impact of Tregs in R2-treated patients and further showed that extra-follicular Treg localization was specifically associated with shorter PFS (HR = 2.87, 95% CI: 1.13-7.28, p = 0.020). These data suggest that high Treg infiltration by mIF is associated with inferior outcome in lenalidomide-treated FL patients and may have potential value for risk stratification.

Biopsy of the lesion revealed ectocervix with an invasive tumour comprising of mononuclear variant and classic Reed-Sternberg cells, and special stains demonstrated CD15, CD30 and Epstein-Barr virus-encoded small RNA (EBER) immunopositivity, in keeping with CHL.
ab: Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) is a rare haematological malignancy that arises from clonal B lymphocytes. Among people living with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), it is the most common non-acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)-defining cancer, with classical Hodgkin lymphoma (CHL) representing the predominant subtype. It is a lymphoid disease, typically involving the axial body lymph nodes, and rarely involving true extranodal sites outside the bone marrow, liver, and spleen. Here we report a rare case of a 41-year-old female, HIV-positive, who presented to multiple healthcare facilities in KwaZulu Natal (KZN), South Africa (SA), treated unsuccessfully for recurrent sexually transmitted infections (STI). Clinical exam revealed a macroscopic cervical mass with the primary suspicion of cervical cancer. Biopsy of the lesion revealed ectocervix with an invasive tumour comprising of mononuclear variant and classic Reed-Sternberg cells, and special stains demonstrated CD15, CD30 and Epstein-Barr virus-encoded small RNA (EBER) immunopositivity, in keeping with CHL.

papers.t: Natural ligand-based CAR T-cell therapy targeting BCMA and TACI for relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma (TriPRIL): a non-randomised, phase 1, first-in-human trial
papers.c: TriPRIL showed a favourable safety profile and warrants further investigation in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, including those previously treated with BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy. The study findings support further development of this dual-targeted, natural ligand-based CAR T-cell approach.
ab: Background

Functional loss of B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) is a recognised mechanism of relapse after BCMA-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma. Targeting multiple tumour antigens simultaneously with a single CAR has the potential to mitigate antigen escape and prolong disease responses. Transmembrane activator and CAML interactor (TACI) and BCMA are both highly expressed on most myeloma cells and bind to the same natural ligand-a proliferation-inducing ligand (APRIL). We designed TriPRIL, a CAR that uses an engineered trimeric form of APRIL, to target both BCMA and TACI. We aimed to establish the safety, tolerability, preliminary efficacy, and recommended phase 2 dose of autologous TriPRIL CAR T cells.
Methods

In this first-in-human, open-label, dose-escalation and dose-expansion, phase 1 study, we evaluated TriPRIL in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma at Massachusetts General Hospital (Boston, MA, USA). Eligible patients had received at least three previous lines of therapy or had triple-class refractory disease. Previous CAR T-cell therapy and bispecific antibody therapy exposure were permitted. Patients received 3 days of lymphodepletion with intravenous cyclophosphamide (300 mg/m2) and intravenous fludarabine (30 mg/m2) daily on days -5, -4, and -3 before intravenous TriPRIL infusion on day 0. In the dose escalation phase, patients received 1·0 × 108 or 3·0 × 108 TriPRIL CAR T cells to establish the recommended phase 2 dose, which was further evaluated in the dose expansion phase. The primary endpoint was the incidence of study-related adverse events (graded according to Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events version 5) and dose-limiting toxicities in all patients who received an infusion of TriPRIL CAR T cells, until study completion at 24 months or progressive disease. The data cutoff date was March 24, 2026, when all infused patients had completed at least one assessment of disease response. This trial was registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05020444), has fully accrued, and is ongoing.
Findings

Between Sept 17, 2021, and Jan 27, 2026, 16 patients were enrolled and underwent leukapheresis, with 15 patients subsequently receiving a TriPRIL cell infusion. Ten (67%) of 15 infused patients were female, five (33%)were male, and the median age was 69 years (IQR 65-75). Nine (60%) of 15 infused patients had previously received BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy, and four (27%) had previously received a BCMA-directed or GPRC5D-directed bispecific T-cell engager. Six patients were treated with 1·0 × 108 CAR T cells, and nine were treated with 3·0 × 108 CAR T cells; there were no dose-limiting toxicities at either dose. The most common adverse events were neutropenia (14 [93%] of 15 patients), nausea (12 [80%]), hypogammaglobulinaemia (eight [53%]), fatigue (seven [47%]), and fever (seven [47%]). Non-haematological adverse events grade 3 or worse occurred in five (33%) patients and all resolved. Cytokine release syndrome (grade 1 or 2 only) occurred in 13 (87%, 95% CI 60-98) infused patients. One (7%, 0-32) patient had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, and one (7%, 0-32) had grade 2 immune effector cell-associated haemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis-like syndrome; both of these patients had received 3·0 × 108 CAR T cells, and both conditions resolved with corticosteroids. Infections occurred in six (40%, 16-68) infused patients, with a grade 3 infection in one patient (7%, 0-32). There were no treatment-related deaths. The recommended phase 2 dose of CAR T cells was set as 3·0 × 108 cells.
Interpretation

TriPRIL showed a favourable safety profile and warrants further investigation in patients with relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma, including those previously treated with BCMA-directed CAR T-cell therapy. The study findings support further development of this dual-targeted, natural ligand-based CAR T-cell approach.

papers.t: Carfilzomib-based strategies in transplant-eligible multiple myeloma: long-term follow-up of the phase 2 FORTE trial
papers.c: In conclusion, long-term follow-up confirms the high effectiveness of KRd-ASCT and KR maintenance. NCT02203643.
ab: In the phase 2 FORTE trial, transplant-eligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma patients aged ≤65 years were randomized to (R1) carfilzomib-lenalidomide-dexamethasone followed by autologous stem cell transplantation (KRd-ASCT), twelve cycles of KRd (KRd12), or carfilzomib-cyclophosphamide-dexamethasone followed by ASCT (KCd-ASCT). Eligible patients were then randomized (R2) to maintenance with carfilzomib for 2 years plus lenalidomide until progression (KR) or lenalidomide alone until progression (R). With extended follow-up (median 99 months from R1 and 85 months from R2), KRd-ASCT significantly increased progression-free survival (PFS, median 98 months) versus KRd12 (median 70 months; HR 0.71, p=0.027) and KCd-ASCT (median 67 months; HR 0.66, p=0.006). A significant benefit in PFS2 was also observed versus both KRd12 (HR 0.65, p=0.02) and KCd-ASCT (HR 0.68, p=0.04) and in terms of overall survival (OS) versus KCd-ASCT (8-year OS: 76% vs 68%; HR 0.65, p=0.04). KR maintenance significantly improved PFS versus R (HR 0.67, p=0.02), with a time-dependent effect persisting up to two years after carfilzomib discontinuation; no differences in PFS2/OS were observed. KR significantly increased rate of measurable residual disease (MRD) conversion (sHR 0.47, p=0.03) during active treatment, and reduced MRD resurgence (sHR 0.53, p=0.001) versus R. Median duration of MRD negativity was 50.5 months in KR vs. 38 months in R arm. MRD-negative patients had significantly prolonged PFS with KR (HR 0.60, p=0.031); MRD-positive patients benefited from KR mainly during carfilzomib therapy (HR 0.46, p=0.05). The cumulative incidence of second primary malignancies was 6%. In conclusion, long-term follow-up confirms the high effectiveness of KRd-ASCT and KR maintenance. NCT02203643.

papers.t: Etentamig in Relapsed/Refractory Multiple Myeloma: Pooled Phase 1 Data of an Investigational BCMA Bispecific Antibody
papers.c: In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). Etentamig's molecular design may be associated with the observed clinical efficacy and tolerability while also potentially supporting extended dosing intervals.
ab: Etentamig is an investigational B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) x CD3 bispecific T-cell engager, composed of a low-affinity CD3 binding domain, potentially reducing cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and infections, a high-avidity bivalent BCMA-binding domain, and retained FcRn binding supporting monthly (Q4W) dosing after a single step-up dose (SUD). We report long-term efficacy and safety from the ongoing, open-label, phase 1 (dose escalation/expansion; NCT03933735) and Arm A of the phase 1b (NCT05650632) studies of etentamig in adult patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma, triple-class exposure, and ≥3 prior lines of therapy (LoT). In phase 1, patients received etentamig 60 mg Q4W or 40 mg Q3W, and in phase 1b, a SUD on Day 1 and 60 mg Q4W on Day 4. Among 146 patients (median age: 68 years; median [range] prior LoT: 4 [3-23]), median follow-up was 13 months (range: 1-48). Objective responses and ≥ very good partial responses occurred in 66% and 54% of patients. Median duration of response and progression-free survival were not reached. Pooled data suggest etentamig has a manageable safety profile, with Grade 3/4 neutropenia and infection occurring in 38% and 23% of patients. In phase 1b Arm A (n=23), overall CRS incidence was 30% (26% Grade 1; 4% Grade 2) with modified dexamethasone premedication and 1 SUD; median onset was 22.3 hours (range: 5.5-29.6) hours, with resolution in 20.7 hours (range: 1.8-131.7). Etentamig's molecular design may be associated with the observed clinical efficacy and tolerability while also potentially supporting extended dosing intervals.

papers.t: Predictive Value of the Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) for Engraftment Syndrome After Autologous Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation in Multiple Myeloma and Lymphoma Patients (EASIX and Engraftment Syndrome in ASCT)
papers.c: While log-transformed EASIX on day 0 correlates with ES risk, its standalone discriminative performance remains modest. EASIX is best utilized as an integrated component within broader, multiparametric risk-stratification models rather than as an isolated predictor.
ab: Engraftment syndrome (ES) is a clinically challenging, hyper-inflammatory complication following autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ASCT). The Endothelial Activation and Stress Index (EASIX) has emerged as a reliable biomarker for endothelial dysfunction and non-relapse mortality in allogeneic transplantation; however, its predictive utility for ES in the autologous setting has not been fully established. This study evaluated the incidence, risk factors, and clinical outcomes of ES in patients with multiple myeloma (MM) and lymphoma, focusing on the dynamic predictive value of peritransplant EASIX scores. We retrospectively analyzed 303 adult patients with MM or lymphoma who underwent ASCT at a single center between 2015 and 2025. ES was diagnosed using the Maiolino criteria. EASIX was assessed at four time points: before conditioning, on the day of transplantation (day 0), and on days +7 and +14. The incidence of ES was 14.2%. Demographic characteristics, conditioning regimens, and infused cell doses did not differ significantly between patients with and without ES. Pre-conditioning EASIX scores were comparable between groups; however, the median EASIX score on day 0 was significantly higher in patients who subsequently developed ES (2.35 vs. 1.46; p = 0.019). In univariable logistic regression, log-transformed EASIX on day 0 was associated with ES development (OR 1.399, 95% CI 1.033-1.894), with an AUC of 0.612 (95% CI 0.524-0.700). Patients with ES had a significantly higher rate of severe (grade 3-4) diarrhea (48.8% vs. 23.1%) and prolonged post-transplant antibiotic therapy (median 12 vs. 8 days). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in progression-free or overall survival. In conclusion, engraftment syndrome significantly increases early post-transplant gastrointestinal toxicity and supportive care requirements without adversely affecting long-term survival outcomes. While log-transformed EASIX on day 0 correlates with ES risk, its standalone discriminative performance remains modest. EASIX is best utilized as an integrated component within broader, multiparametric risk-stratification models rather than as an isolated predictor.

ab: Daratumumab, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (DRd) is a standard first-line treatment for transplant-ineligible newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (TIE-NDMM). We retrospectively evaluated 268 patients treated with DRd at nine Japanese institutions. The overall and complete response rates were 90.6% and 28.9%, respectively. At a median follow-up of 22.2 months, 2-year progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival were 74.6% and 86.2%. PFS in patients with t(11;14) tended to be shorter than that in those without t(11;14) (hazard ratio [HR], 1.483; p = 0.139). Two-year PFS differed across R2-ISS stages I-IV (94.1%, 82.2%, 74.6%, and 68.1%; log-rank p = 0.002). Among 208 patients with complete six-group cytogenetic classification, t(11;14) with del(17p) and/or 1q21 abnormalities (n = 16) was associated with shorter PFS than the reference cytogenetic group in an exploratory comparison (HR, 2.470; p = 0.042). These findings indicate that coexisting cytogenetic abnormalities may modify the prognostic implications of t(11;14) with numerical cytogenetic abnormalities, requiring validation in larger cohorts.

Immune effector cell associated hematotoxicity (ICAHT) with BCMA CAR T cell therapy in the earlier lines
papers.c: Early-line CAR T-cell therapy was associated with superior 12-month PFS (87.8% vs 65.4%) and OS (96.2% vs 85.9%). These real-world data show that ICAHT occurs even with earlier-line BCMA CAR T-cell therapy, though less severe, and underscore the prognostic importance of early post-infusion cytopenias.
ab: B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA)-directed chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy is highly effective in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (MM), but adverse effects such as immune effector cell-associated hematotoxicity (ICAHT) remain a challenging early and long-term toxicity. Most reports on ICAHT originate from CAR T-cell therapies in late-stage MM, with limited data from earlier-line treatment. We conducted a multi-institutional retrospective study of 245 MM patients treated with BCMA CAR T, comparing ICAHT between early-line [early CAR T] (1-3 prior lines; n = 69) and late-line [late CAR T] (≥4 prior lines; n = 176) cohorts. Cytopenias (neutropenia ≤1000/µL, thrombocytopenia ≤50,000/µL, anemia ≤9 g/dL) were assessed at day 21 (D + 21), 3, and 6 months post-CAR T-cell infusion. At D + 21, ICAHT was less frequent with early CAR T versus late CAR T (39% vs 62%; p = 0.002), driven largely by lower thrombocytopenia (17% vs 39%; p = 0.001). At 3 months, ICAHT remained more common with late CAR T (30% vs 12%; p = 0.004), but by 6 months, rates converged (8.9% vs 18%; p = 0.126). Blood counts among patients with ICAHT at D + 21 often remained inferior at 3 and 6 months despite stem cell boosts. ICAHT at D + 21 independently predicted worse overall survival (HR 3.12; p = 0.022). Early-line CAR T-cell therapy was associated with superior 12-month PFS (87.8% vs 65.4%) and OS (96.2% vs 85.9%). These real-world data show that ICAHT occurs even with earlier-line BCMA CAR T-cell therapy, though less severe, and underscore the prognostic importance of early post-infusion cytopenias.

ab: Patient-reported outcome (PRO) and quality of life (QoL) assessments for multiple myeloma (MM) patients are traditionally collected at infrequent intervals using burdensome instruments, resulting in limited clinical visibility between visits. This creates a critical gap in care, as evolving symptoms and treatment-related toxicities frequently occur outside scheduled encounters and may remain unrecognized. A single-centre pilot study evaluated the feasibility and clinical utility of a short message service (SMS)-based remote monitoring platform, assessing 8 symptoms and 10 QoL domains for 58 MM patients over 90 days. End-points included feasibility and engagement measured using completion rates, time burden and identification of clinically actionable events. A total of 1604 assessments were delivered, with an overall completion rate of 85.5%, and 72.4% of participants achieving >80% completion rate. Median completion time was 1.80 min. During the 90-day study period, 215 predefined alerts were generated, of which 101 (47.0%) prompted clinical intervention within 48 h, frequently occurring outside routine clinic visits. SMS-based remote monitoring demonstrated high feasibility, sustained engagement and minimal patient burden. This platform enabled real-time identification of symptoms and facilitated rapid follow-up by clinicians, supporting its potential for remote therapeutic monitoring rather than a passive data collection tool.
